angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 769,444 km at 108.69 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.2009 +/- 0.0144 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 108.69 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.106 +/- 0.051 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5726.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 769,444 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.06 +/- 0.13 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5726.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5874 +/- 119 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5726.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5726.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5726.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.376, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5726 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.11832, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1097091022864217472, flags_flame 00: age_flame 8.227073 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 7.1650944 to 9.284129)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
